strategy.title: Follow-Through Day (FTD)
strategy.text: Qualification Requirements A valid Follow-Through Day requires a gain of 1.0% or greater on higher volume than the prior session on either the NASDAQ Composite or S&P 500, occurring on Day 4 or later of an official rally attempt.

strategy.title: Tentative Nature of Early Signals
strategy.text: Should a Follow-Through Day materialize during Friday's shortened session or early next week, investors must treat it as an initial signal to deploy pilot capital ("dip the toe in the water") rather than an aggressive "all-in" buy regime.

strategy.title: Technical Quality Constraints
strategy.text: An FTD generated below key moving average lines (such as the 200-day SMA or 21-day EMA) or beneath prior pivot lows carries a higher failure rate than a breakout out of a power base.

strategy.title: Risk Guardrails
strategy.text: The absolute low of the Follow-Through Day session serves as the immediate stop-loss line in the sand. A close below the FTD low invalidates the rally attempt and mandates an immediate return to cash. Portfolio Exposure & Volatility-Adjusted Position Sizing In high-ATR market environments (where individual growth stocks feature 7% to 10% daily price swings), traditional position sizing must be scaled back significantly: 1. Pilot Sizing: Limit initial position sizes to 2% to 3% of total portfolio capital (or half-positions) to prevent capital erosion during intraday whipsaws. 2. ATR-Based Stop Placement: Account for wider stock-specific volatility bands (e.g., JROG's 9.5% ATR) by setting logical stop losses beneath weekly moving average support rather than tight intraday stops that invite shakeouts. 3. Patience for Base Maturation: Focus exclusively on equities maintaining RS lines near high ground (such as CHYM, CDNA, and JROG), allowing V-shaped intraday swings to settle into proper, multi-week consolidation patterns before expanding exposure.

Navigating volatile market bottoms requires strict adherence to quantitative risk rules, formal follow-through day criteria, and structured execution protocols.

strategy.title: The Follow-Through Day (FTD)
strategy.text: Protocol A Follow-Through Day represents the single most reliable historical signal marking a systemic shift from a market correction to a new uptrend:.

strategy.title: Timing Window
strategy.text: Can occur no earlier than Day 4 of a rally attempt. Day 1 was established on Monday, November 23; Day 0 (the rally low established on Friday, November 20) represents the absolute line in the sand that must not be undercut.

strategy.title: Price & Volume Requirements
strategy.text: Requires an index gain of 1.25% or greater on the NASDAQ Composite or S&P 500, accompanied by total session volume heavier than the prior session.

strategy.title: Holiday Session Nuance
strategy.text: Day 4 of the current rally attempt falls on Black Friday (a shortened trading session following Thanksgiving). Achieving higher total volume on a short session is statistically improbable unless distorted by penny stock volume. Therefore, an advance on Black Friday may represent an "FTD in spirit," but institutional confirmation will likely require a traditional FTD during the following trading week.

strategy.title: Failure Management
strategy.text: Over 50% of historical Follow-Through Days ultimately fail. A close below the low of the FTD session immediately invalidates the buy signal and mandates raising cash exposure. Three-Phase Trend Change Checklist To complement Follow-Through Day rules, institutional traders utilize a three-phase Trend Change Checklist: 1. Closing Price Above Moving Average: Must achieve a daily close above the target line (21-day, 50-day, or 200-day). 2. Intraday Low Above Moving Average: Daily low must remain above the moving average while closing positive on the session. 3. Three-Day Confirmation Rule: Must maintain daily lows above the moving average while closing positive for 3 consecutive sessions. Execution Strategy & Cash Management 1. Maintain Cash Posture During Day 1 Bounces: Active traders should remain 100% in cash or held long-term positions during initial explosive snapback days, avoiding the temptation to chase momentum without trend confirmation. 2. Build and Merge Sector Watchlists: Screen the database for equities holding above their 50-day and 200-day moving averages with daily volume exceeding $20 million. Group focus lists by industry sector to identify emerging accumulation clusters. 3. Monitor Relative Strength Divergences: Focus capital exclusively on equities whose RS lines make new high ground ahead of broad market index recoveries.
